claim: Published positive effects shrink on independent high-powered replication: about half the effect size, and roughly 36-62% still significant, across psychology, economics and Nature/Science social science.
agent_test: Re-run our claimed gains from the selection stage on fresh items; expect about half the effect and report the shrinkage ratio.

claim: Replication success rates: OSC 35/97 (36%), Many Labs 2 15/28 (54%), Camerer 2016 11/18 (61%), Camerer 2018 13/21 (62%). Effect ratios: OSC r 0.40 to 0.20, ML2 median d 0.60 to 0.15, econ 0.66, N/S 0.46.
agent_test: Use 0.5 as the default shrink factor for any in-sample gain until confirmed on held-out data.

claim: Lower original p-value and simple (not interaction) effects replicate more often: original p<.001 replicated 63%, p>.04 replicated 18%; main effects 47% vs interactions 22%.
agent_test: Require a larger margin (more items, tighter interval) for borderline gains; compare replication of large vs marginal margins.

claim: Hidden moderators (sample, setting, task order) explain little of non-replication; heterogeneity is small and sits in real, large effects.
agent_test: When a gain fails on a new item set, do not accept 'context differs' without testing the named moderator.

claim: Peer forecasts of replication are informative: Nature/Science markets 63.4% and survey 60.6% vs observed 61.9%; markets overshot in economics (75.2% vs 61.1%).
agent_test: Have the agent forecast the chance each claim holds on held-out data, log it, and score calibration (Brier) across runs.

claim: Chance a positive claim is true falls with low pre-study odds, low power, many tested relationships and flexible analysis (PPV 0.85 down to 0.001 in Ioannidis Table 4). This is a model, not an empirical rate.
agent_test: Count candidates tried per answer; discount a surprising winner by search width; test the selected-vs-fresh gap at equal tokens.

claim: Researcher flexibility inflates false positives (Simmons: combined practices about 61% at p<.05, not re-verified; Head: excess of p-values just under .05; John: QRPs common by self-report).
agent_test: Freeze the scoring and stopping rule in the scaffold; compare false-gain rate with and without freezing.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Publication bias: in the TESS cohort 10/48 null results were published vs 56/91 strongly significant; most of the gap is authors not writing up nulls.
agent_test: Log failed attempts and surface them at the final-answer stage; test whether this lowers overconfidence.

claim: Low power gives inflated estimates (winner's curse): Button 2013 page abstract gives neuroscience median power of about 8% to 31% depending on subfield. The earlier 21% is not on the page that could be opened; use the range.
agent_test: Report the held-out score of the selected candidate, not the selection score; measure the gap vs number of candidates.

claim: The OSC headline rate is contested: Gilbert et al. argue statistical errors and high reproducibility; OSC authors replied; the definition of success drives the figure.
agent_test: Use several indicators (direction, interval, pooled estimate), not one pass/fail.

claim: A p-value alone is not a measure of truth (ASA 2016, six principles). Benjamin 2018 (re-read): p=0.05 equals Bayes factor about 2.5-3.4, p=0.005 equals about 14-26; with prior odds 1:10 and p<0.05 the false positive rate exceeds 33% at any power, 5% at p<0.005.
agent_test: Replace pass/fail on one comparison with effect size plus interval and a pre-set margin.

claim: Analytic reproducibility with data and code is imperfect: 18/28 ML-challenge papers fully reproduced, 128/203 economics, 311/601 CS, 16/25 psychology (Hardwicke 2021).
agent_test: Make the agent execute the check instead of recalling a result; log re-run failure rate.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Preclinical cancer biology: median effect 85% smaller than original; 0 of 193 experiments described fully enough to design a protocol; raw data shared for 16%.
agent_test: Have the agent write method text a stranger could run; score completeness.

claim: Agents are weak at full replication from text: PaperBench best 21.0% (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, BasicAgent) vs humans 41.4% best-of-3 on a 3-paper subset (o1 26.6%); most models finish early and claim completion.
agent_test: Add a forced check that claimed work was run; compare success with and without it at equal tokens.

claim: Scaffold effects are model-specific: IterativeAgent raised o1 from 13.2 to 24.4% but lowered Claude 3.5 Sonnet from 21.0 to 16.1% on PaperBench.
agent_test: Test every loop change per base model; assume no transfer.

claim: CORE-Bench: with code and data, best agent 60/57.8/21.5% (easy/medium/hard); task hints lift a general agent; newer coding agents solve most rerun tasks (Claude Code 93.4% task accuracy on SocSci-Repro).
agent_test: Compare plain vs scaffolded agent on rerun tasks at equal tokens; hints and checklists are the scaffold part.

claim: Agents anchor on the expected answer: with the target paper, accuracy on non-reproducible tasks fell from 100 to 63.3% (Claude Code) and 100 to 90% (Codex); confirmatory prompting cut it to about 70% and 60%.
agent_test: Include impossible items; measure correct 'cannot be done' rate with and without the target shown and with goal-pressure wording.

claim: Judging whether a study holds is harder than rerunning its code: REPRO-Bench best existing agent 21.4% (below 25% chance); a fallback-first scaffold gave 36.6%.
agent_test: Test a write-fallback-then-verify step on judging tasks at equal tokens.

claim: LLM annotation and prompt choice are researcher degrees of freedom: wrong conclusion in about 31% of hypotheses (SOTA) to 50% (small models); false positive achievable for 94.4% of nulls; 100 human labels cut Type I to about 10%. Judges are prompt-sensitive too: rewording the judge instruction lowers verdict agreement by 0.034 to 0.181 across four tasks (25 judges, JudgeSense).
agent_test: Fix prompt and model before looking; test paraphrase robustness of each answer; supply a small trusted check set.

claim: LLM simulated samples are not independent replications: GPT replicated 37.5% of 8 studies with near-zero variance (99.6% 'conservative'); Saynova F1 up to 77% but varies with temperature; Aher found good replication in some tasks and hyper-accuracy in wisdom of crowds.
agent_test: Measure answer diversity across samples; do not count self-consistency votes from one model as independent evidence.

claim: Single runs are noisy: at temperature 0 accuracy varied by up to 15% across runs; benchmark comparisons from one seed give either about 10% false positives or low power; pass@8 doubles pass@1 on MLE-bench (16.9 to 34.1%).
agent_test: Run at least 3 seeds per arm; treat gains inside run-to-run range as zero; report pass@1 and pass@k separately.

claim: Prompt format drives LLM survey answers: after randomizing option order, answers of 43 models trend toward uniform.
agent_test: Shuffle answer options in every choice test; count a result only if stable.

claim: Independent analysis paths agree on direction far more often than magnitude: LLM reproduction same conclusion 80%, effect within 0.05 d only 24%; sign agreement 75-91%.
agent_test: Use agreement of independent routes as a direction check; do not trust exact numbers from one route.

claim: Autonomous AI-scientist output has many faults: 5 of 12 experiments failed from coding errors, hallucinated numbers, weak literature review (small sample).
agent_test: Add a check that every reported number traces to an executed output.

claim: Graded closeness beats pass/fail for tracking progress (A to F bands by percent difference); stage-wise scoring shows where pipelines break (ReplicatorBench: strong code execution, weak data retrieval).
agent_test: Score intermediate artifacts, not only the final answer, in our evals.

claim: Selecting the best of many candidates by a self-scored metric overstates the gain, and the overstatement grows with the number of candidates and shrinks with the number of scoring items. Pre-registered loop study: selection score exceeded held-out by 13-20 points at 16 items and 1-5 points at 256. Simulation: +1.5 pp at 3 candidates, +4.0 pp at 50 identical candidates; identical systems declared winner up to 94% of the time.
agent_test: At equal tokens, report selected-candidate score on held-out items beside the selection score; expect about 15 points of inflation with 16 items.

claim: Most later proposals in a self-improvement loop are harmful: only 4-39% of rewrites after the first improve on the incumbent; greedy at n=16 ends below the seed in half of seeds while its own score rises 12.5 points.
agent_test: Do not keep a change because its score went up on the same few items; require a paired test on fresh items.

claim: A small never-used audit set removes the average bias of a loop's reported gain: 64 fresh items (128 evaluations, one tenth of the budget) cut RMSE of reported gain from 15.5 to 5.7 points, but single estimates stay about 6 points off.
agent_test: Reserve about 64 unseen items to score the start and the final prompt; report gain with an interval.

claim: Acceptance rules set in advance (sequential tests, McNemar, Bayes gate) sharply cut false commits and churn (greedy 72-100% false commits with no real gain; 13 edits per run vs under 1), but over whole runs they did not reliably raise held-out accuracy. The PACE degradation did not replicate in Hu and Tang's pre-registered runs.
agent_test: A frozen decision rule is good hygiene, not a proven accuracy booster. Measure both churn and held-out gain.

claim: Judge-based comparison is itself a measurement with error: rewording a judge prompt shifts verdicts (JSS -0.034 to -0.181), siblings from one vendor are not independent (clustered SEs 1.37-1.63 times larger), and a small human-labelled set (n=100) can calibrate judge TPR/FPR to give valid tests.
agent_test: Use two judge wordings and judges from more than one vendor; check the judge against about 100 human labels.

claim: Detecting a 3 point paired gain needs several hundred to about 1,400 items depending on how often the two systems disagree (derived: about 690 at 10% disagreement, about 1,370 at 20%). Small pilots only see large effects.
agent_test: Do not claim a 3-point scaffold gain from fewer than a few hundred paired items; state the minimum detectable gain.

claim: Which gains survive depends on size and task: large gains from weak starting prompts (26-39 points) persist at every selection size; small gains of a few points are inside selection noise; larger selection sets help on TREC but not GSM8K. Harness evolution beats matched-budget search on game tasks (+80% ARC-AGI-3, +11% EdgeBench) but not on Terminal-Bench.
agent_test: Trust large margins; re-test marginal ones on fresh items; always run a matched-compute baseline.

claim: A frozen-control arm measured through the same pipeline is needed to find phantom gains: a frozen Qwen3-8B shows an apparent expansion rate of 0.280 from decode noise alone; seven measurement failures each reverse a reported finding without the null.
agent_test: Re-run the unchanged agent as a control and report the same statistic on it.

claim: A verify-before-claim stage with a model verifier raised shipped precision (median 0.471 vs 0.353, pre-registered, 20 runs) with recall not significantly different but non-inferiority on retained true candidates not met (lower bound 0.875 vs floor 0.90). Abstract-level only.
agent_test: Add a separate verifier before claims ship; track retained true findings so the verifier does not suppress real ones.

claim: Samples from one model are only partly independent: candidate errors correlate 0.44-0.60 and the correction error shared by all candidates remains. No direct study of vote accuracy against measured diversity was found.
agent_test: Treat repeated samples as correlated; mix prompts or models before counting agreement as replication.
